outcomes.title: An operator signs in and reaches the control plane
criteria: The dashboard accepts an access token and shows the primary navigation and the Work view

outcomes.title: An operator creates work and finds it where they look
criteria: A created work item is listed in the work list
A created work item appears in the board's backlog group

outcomes.title: An operator reads an item's criteria and gates
criteria: An item's page shows its criteria, proofs and gates by id and by key

outcomes.title: An operator sees what is tested and whether it passes
criteria: The Tests page lists every case with its recent runs

outcomes.title: A repository onboarded the normal way gets the rapid delivery path by default
criteria: After a normal install and init of a repository, the project's delivery settings show local previews, candidates of at most five changes, and required production verification, without any extra setup step
The project runs the local preview and candidate path with no GitHub Actions workflow and no Railway preview environment; GitHub remains an optional asynchronous mirror
The user and operator docs under docs/ describe these defaults, how a project declares its applications and cases, and what happens when a candidate fails

outcomes.title: A proposed change gets its own local preview the team can open and judge
criteria: A change whose declared application case needs a preview gets one without anyone asking for it
The item shows the preview link and its state, and the declared application case's result from running in that preview
Opening the preview link shows the change itself running — the site serves this change's content, not a placeholder

outcomes.title: Every preview runs alone — its own state and database, no production secrets — and cleans up after itself
criteria: Two previews running at the same time each report their own state identity and their own database, both on the preview page the team opens and on the item's record
The previewed application receives no production credentials, and the item's preview record lists none
When a change is settled its preview is cleaned up automatically: the item records the cleanup with a time, the preview link stops serving, and other previews keep running

outcomes.title: Both a declared static site and a declared Compose app get working local previews, with no Railway or GitHub Actions
criteria: A change needing the static site gets a preview that serves the site with the change visible on it
A change needing the Compose-backed application gets a preview that serves the running application against its own database
Both previews are served by Graphyard locally — the item names the local runner — with no Railway preview environment and no GitHub Actions workflow involved

outcomes.title: Ready changes batch into a small exact candidate — at most five — that names exactly what it contains
criteria: A candidate names each change it contains by work item and by that change's merge commit, and carries one exact source identity for the whole batch
A batch never contains more than five changes
A change that becomes ready after a full batch waits for the next candidate and is the whole of it

outcomes.title: Only a candidate whose combined required cases pass is promoted; a failed candidate never promotes and its failure stays on record
criteria: A candidate whose combined required end-to-end cases pass is promoted, and the delivery view shows production expecting that candidate's release bound to its member's exact merge commit
A candidate whose combined required cases fail is not promoted, and the candidate record names the failed cases
Production keeps the previous passing candidate's release, and the failed candidate's record with its failure stays readable afterwards

outcomes.title: Production is verified to run exactly the promoted candidate, and drift is caught
criteria: The delivery view shows the live production environment observed running the promoted candidate's release id and exact source, not just that some release is out there
Verification reads 'verified' only while the live environment runs that exact release
When the live environment serves something else, verification turns to a mismatch that says so, while the expected release still names the promoted candidate
